answer: A registry that charges a refundable stake in a scarce resource resists sybils: each identity must lock a deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so an attacker pays linearly per fake identity while honest agents recover theirs. Add a pearl-like reputation bond that only vests after verifiable work, a juniper-tree web of trust where existing members vouch with their own stake, and walnut-hard rate limits on new identities per epoch. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand stakes, not one script.
